Therefore, the results in Figure 8.1a indicate that there seems to be no correlation between temperature and device stability (Milestone 1.2.4). Inspecting the 85°C aged devices individually in Figure 8.1b, there seems to be a large variation in stability among each of the 4 devices. We further observed “white spots” dotting after thermal aging (Figure 8.1c). We suspect that the “white spots” are some forms of impurity (and/or pinhole) that was already originally present within the fresh devices (possibly introduced during fabrication) and was responsible for catalyzing/accelerating the device degradation under thermal stress. The gold diffusion into devices, for example, would be accelerated because of the pinhole. This intrinsic thermal stability of our new simplified spiro-MeOTAD might be still sufficient to withstand heating at 85 °C. To further verify the argument, we are currently testing 16 of our simplified spiro structure devices made using TPPO as a barrier layer under 85 °C. The champion device as shown in green maintains its initial efficiency (~20%) after 225 hours of aging. On average, these devices retain 92% of its initial efficiency after 225 hours of aging (Figure 8.2), which shows some improvement in stability. In terms of humidity stability, we exposed encapsulated devices to different humidity environments of relative humidity (RH) 0% (nitrogen glovebox), RH 1-5% (dry box), RH 20-50% (ambient atmosphere), and RH 85% (oven). The devices are encapsulated with a UV-curable epoxy resin and edge-sealed glass piece in nitrogen. Figure 8.3 plots the average PCEs (absolute values) of 4 devices each at the different RH environment. The devices showed no obvious degradation for up to 576 hours when aged in RH 0%, or RH 1-5%, or RH 20-50%. Only the devices aged in RH 85% showed noticeable degradation, where its PCE declined to ~68% of its initial value after 360 hours of ageing. It is not clear to us why only the RH 85% environment affects the device stability, but it is likely due to failure of the encapsulation. More generally, it is understood that humidity stability is more often just a test of the robustness of the encapsulation itself, rather than the intrinsic humidity resistance of the solar cell stack.
